# @tiavision/sinter-mail

> Email bodies in a sinter app, without an iframe: `mail.parse(html, options)` turns an email's HTML into a sanitized tree (the browser's own tree construction, every element's CSS resolved), `mail.plain(text, options)` does the same for plain text, and `<mail-body data-sn-with="{ body }">` renders the tree as part of the page. Pure helpers: an email in a `file:` resource is plain HTML at build time.

Setup: `sinter({ libraries: ['@tiavision/sinter-mail'] })`; `export * as mail from '@tiavision/sinter-mail'` in src/sinter.helpers.ts; `export type { Body, Element } from '@tiavision/sinter-mail'` in src/sinter.types.ts. Lazy parser: also `lazy: ['@tiavision/sinter-mail']` (a let over mail.parse is undefined until it loads).

- `mail.parse(html, { images, proxy, cid, media, dataImages })`: `images` 'block' (default: remote images left out, their box kept) | 'allow' | 'proxy' (with `proxy: '/img?url={url}'`, `{url}` once); `cid` a map `{ 'id@host': url }` or a template with `{cid}`; `media` 'wide' (800 px, default) | 'narrow' (375 px), the width `@media` rules are evaluated at; `dataImages` the largest data: image kept (characters, default 65536). Invalid options throw. Same source and options give the same frozen tree.
- `mail.plain(text, { flowed, delsp })`: paragraphs, autolinks, `>` quotes (class mail-quote), `-- ` signature (class mail-signature); `flowed` for format=flowed.
- `mail.text(node)`: the text, for previews. `mail.links(body)`: every link with its text.
- `<mail-body>` leaves out what the email hides at the parsed width (`display: none`, and all inside it): its images never load. Parse again with the other `media` when the reader's width crosses a breakpoint: `<mail-width data-sn-on-media="media = $event.detail">` beside the `<mail-body>` emits `'wide'`/`'narrow'` (640 px, prop `breakpoint`) when first laid out and at each crossing; state `{ media: /** @type {'wide' | 'narrow' | null} */ (null) }` and `media ? mail.parse(html, { media }) : null`: parsed once, for the right width (starting at 'wide' parses twice on a phone and requests the desktop images).
- `body.light`: the email sets colours of its own and does not say they work on a dark page; `<mail-body>` then puts `mail-light` on its root. `import '@tiavision/sinter-mail/mail.css'` (optional): the browser defaults emails count on back under `.mail` for apps with a CSS reset (tables and images as drawn, `content-box`, block margins, images no wider than the reader), `.mail-light` a light canvas, `.mail-scroll` a box that scrolls a wide email sideways.
- Quoted history and signatures: `part: 'quote'`/`'signature'` (classes mail-quote, mail-signature) from Gmail (`gmail_quote`, `gmail_signature`), Apple Mail and Thunderbird (`blockquote type="cite"`, `moz-cite-prefix`, `moz-signature`), Outlook (from `#appendonsend`/`#divRplyFwdMsg`/its header block to the end of the parent, wrapped in one div; `#Signature`), new Outlook, Yahoo, Proton; `body.quotes` when there is history. `mail.unquoted(body)`: a copy without it (the body itself when nothing is quoted or nothing would be left); `mail.progressive(mail.unquoted(tree))`.
- `body.images.origins`: the origins of the remote images, for a "show images from …" control. A 1 × 1 (or smaller) image, a tracking pixel, is left out of the tree and of `origins`.
- `body.schemes`: `['light', 'dark']` and the like when the email declares its colour schemes (`color-scheme` meta or property, `supported-color-schemes`); `dark` also when it has `prefers-color-scheme: dark` rules, whose colours are written `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` and follow the scheme the body is shown in. Absent: written for a white page (keep it light on a dark page: `color-scheme: light` around it).
- `<mail-body>` slots: `link` (`$slot.node`, its children through `<slot></slot>`) and `image` (`$slot.node.attrs.src` absent when blocked).
- `mail.progressive(tree)`: a numbered copy (the tree itself is not changed, so a frozen mail.parse tree goes in as it is; the same tree gives the same copy): `<mail-body data-sn-with="{ body: mail.progressive(tree) }">` renders a long body progressively, its first 200 nodes first, the rest in steps of 5 to 15 ms after a paint; a body not numbered renders whole (static pages stay script-free).

Styles: the email's own win over the page's (inline); the page fills in what the email does not set (fonts, link colours). Kept: colours, fonts, text, box, borders, tables, display, float. Never: position, url(), web fonts, :hover, negative margins.

CSP: rendered in the browser, nothing beyond `script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'`. Folded at build time (file: emails): `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`.

Security: nothing runs (no script, handler, javascript: link, SVG, form, iframe), nothing loads without the app (images blocked or through its proxy, no CSS url()), nothing leaves the email's box, no class or stylesheet reaches the page, ids only for in-email links (prefixed mail-), `role` only as `presentation`/`none` on a layout table.

Guide: docs/mail.md. Design: docs/proposals/sinter-mail.md.
